questions.prompt: How far does Keating say Voyager 2 has gone relative to the nearest star?
choices: A One light day from Earth; the nearest star is over four light years away.
B Four light years already, past Proxima.
C Halfway to Andromeda.
D Still inside Earth orbit only.
questions.explain: Voyager 2 is ~1 light-day out; nearest star ~4+ light years.

questions.prompt: What is one parsec, as Keating defines it in the distance-ladder discussion?
choices: A A unit of time equal to one Earth year.
B A distance measure tied to a 1 AU baseline and a one-arcsecond parallax angle.
C The mass of the Sun.
D The brightness of Vega.
questions.explain: Parsec is defined via the AU baseline and parallax geometry.

questions.prompt: Keating notes Earth is tilted by about how many degrees relative to the ecliptic, producing seasons?
choices: A Exactly 0° (no tilt).
B About 23°.
questions.explain: He states ~23° tilt with respect to the ecliptic and links it to seasons.

questions.prompt: Roughly what minimum fraction of the Sun's mass does Keating say an object needs to be considered a star (capable of fusion)?
choices: A About 1–2% of the Sun's mass.
B About 8% of the Sun's mass.
C Exactly 100% of the Sun's mass.
D Jupiter's mass is enough.
questions.explain: He says you need ~8% of the Sun's mass; Jupiter cannot fuse.

questions.prompt: What detection method does Keating describe as a miniature eclipse when a planet crosses its star?
choices: A Only gravitational lensing of quasars.
B The transit method.
C Neutrino counting alone.
D Measuring Earth's tides.
questions.explain: He calls the transit a miniature eclipse/transit method for exoplanets.
